rounds.text: ASM Technologies is delivering exceptional top-line and bottom-line expansion, evidenced by a 3-year compounded sales growth of 34% and a trailing twelve month sales growth of 57% [E16, E17]. Profitability is scaling at an even faster pace, highlighted by a 3-year compounded profit growth of 87% and a TTM profit growth of 53% [E20, E21]. This hyper-growth is structurally backed by significant operational leverage, as operating margins expanded by 18 percentage points over three years to reach 21% in the TTM period [E30], alongside strong cash generation where operating cash flow of Rs 68 Cr fully backs reported profits at a 1.11x conversion rate for March 2026 [E34, E35]. Furthermore, institutional backing is growing rapidly with domestic institutions increasing their stake by 6.88 percentage points since March 2024, driving positive institutional money flow [E43, E44]. The company's high quality of earnings is validated by strong returns on capital, featuring an ROE of 25.5% [E13] and an ROCE of 27.0% [E12], vastly outperforming the sector median ROCE of 12.6% [E68]. Conceded: the stock trades at an elevated P/E of 109x with free cash flow sitting at negative Rs 25 Cr for March 2026 [E1, E36].

ASM Technologies Ltd trades at an extreme valuation that is entirely detached from its fundamental intrinsic value, carrying a P/E ratio of 109x against a sector benchmark of just 19.75x [E1, E6]. This exorbitant pricing is further underscored by a price-to-book ratio of 26.07x and an EV/EBITDA of 72.43x, both of which tower over their respective sector benchmarks of 1.96x and 10.64x [E2, E7, E11]. A discounted cash flow model explicitly flags this disconnect, placing intrinsic value at Rs 2,430 per share compared to the market price of Rs 6,310, resulting in a negative margin of safety of -159.6% [E45, E46]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that today's market price already demands an aggressive 31.4% earnings growth rate, far outstripping the 18.0% growth assumed in the base case [E47]. Balance sheet metrics also deteriorate under scrutiny, with free cash flow sitting deeply negative at Rs -25 Cr and total borrowings rising significantly to Rs 209 Cr in Sep 2026 from Rs 128 Cr a year prior [E36, E39]. Compounding these risk factors, promoter holdings have compressed by 8.05 percentage points since March 2024, dropping to 53.49% by October 2026 [E41]. conceded: [E14], [E15], [E16], [E17], [E18], [E19], [E20], [E21]

The bear's valuation critique relies on static multiples that completely ignore the company's hyper-accelerating fundamental velocity, evidenced by TTM sales growth surging 57% and profit growth hitting 53% [E17, E21]. While the bear highlights DCF and multiple disconnects [E1, E2, E7, E11, E45, E46, E47], it overlooks that results are accelerating with a perfect 100/100 score and net profit soaring 79% YoY [E64]. The cited negative free cash flow [E36] is countered by robust operating cash flow of Rs 68 Cr and a healthy 1.11x cash conversion ensuring profits are fully backed by cash [E34, E35], alongside a comfortable short-term liquidity current ratio of 2.61x [E38]. Although borrowings rose [E39], the company's elite return profile featuring a 27.0% ROCE and 25.5% ROE dwarfs sector benchmarks [E8, E9, E10, E12, E13]. Furthermore, institutional investors are aggressively backing this growth with a positive money flow and a 5.83 percentage point increase in holdings [E44]. conceded: [E1], [E2], [E7], [E11], [E36], [E39], [E41], [E45], [E46], [E47].

The bull dismisses the valuation multiples [E1, E2, E7, E11], but ignores that a P/E of 105.34x and EV/EBITDA of 72.43x dwarf sector benchmarks of 19.75x and 10.64x by immense margins [E6, E11]. The reverse DCF proves that the current price of ₹6,310 already demands an improbable 31.4% earnings growth—far higher than the 18.0% base case—resulting in a staggering margin of safety of -159.6% against the intrinsic value of ₹2,430 [E45, E46, E47]. While the bull defends cash generation via operating cash flow [E34, E35], it glosses over negative free cash flow of Rs -25 Cr [E36] and surging borrowings climbing to Rs 209 Cr from Rs 128 Cr [E39]. Furthermore, insider confidence is visibly waning as promoter holdings dropped 8.05 percentage points from Mar 2024 to Oct 2026, including a 4.16% reduction just in the last quarter [E41, E56]. conceded: [E17, E21, E34, E35, E38].
